newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Suria down on rumours of dropped merger.
newsitem.headline: Suria down on rumours of dropped merger.

text.p: Suria Capital Bhd fell sharply in active trade on Monday morning on rumours that central Bank Negara was against the company proceeding with merger talks with MBf Capital Bhd, dealers said.
At 0232 GMT Suria was down 10 cents, or 3.6 percent, to 2.65 ringgit with 4.7 million shares traded.
MBf Capital share remained suspended following the submission to Bank Negara for merger talks to start last week.
"The stock has come off on the talk that Bank Negara has objected to the merger talks proceeding," said Irene Tan, head of research at Vickers Ballas.

A report in The Edge, a weekly financial publication, on Monday quoted banking sources as saying that the central bank had recommended to the Ministry of Finance that permission not be granted to the two parties to proceed with merger talks.

Officials at Suria Capital were not immediately available for comment. An official at MBf Capital said, "As yet, we cannot comment on rumours." Officials at Bank Negara could not immediately be reached for comment.
Rumours surfaced nearly two months ago that MBf Capital and Suria Capital could be looking at some form of merger, primarily concerning Suria's subsidiary Sabah Bank Bhd.
A merger between the groups would result in MBf Capital holding a banking licence, while Suria would gain significant financial clout, analysts said.
